therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: adults with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular risk factors enrolled in the ACCORD trial
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: number of participants with at least one non-vertebral fracture and number of participants with at least one fall

results.effect_size: HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.86–1.27) for non-vertebral fracture; RR 1.10 (95% CI 0.84–1.43) for falls

context.indication: type 2 diabetes with cardiovascular risk factors—skeletal health outcomes (fractures, falls, height loss)
context.duration: average follow-up 3.8 years for fractures, 2.0 years for falls, 5 years for height loss
context.investigator_commentary: The BONE ancillary study was initiated during recruitment for the main ACCORD trial. Intensive glycemic control did not significantly reduce non-vertebral fractures (HR 1.04, p=0.678), falls (RR 1.10, p=0.490), or height loss >2 cm (OR 0.99, p=0.854) compared to standard glycemic control.
